title: Brokerage House Initial Public Offerings and Analyst Forecast Quality
eligible_reason: Staggered binary treatment: analysts/brokerages are treated around their brokerage's IPO date, which differs across brokerages (IBES broker panel over 31 years; 762 brokers in the broker-year regressions). The headline forecast-level DiD (Tables 3-5, 9-11) includes time-varying analyst controls in every column (ineligible). Table 7 columns 7-9 regress broker-year outcomes (ln_numfirms, ln_numanalyst, ln_numforecast) on ipo_prepost1 with broker and year FE and no controls, which satisfies the regression rules. Caveat: ipo_prepost1 is a two-year window indicator (year before and year after the IPO) that reverts to 0 afterwards, so the Hull switch-off rule (drop post-adoption periods with treatment = 0) must be applied; the adoption date is the IPO year minus one. The analysis data are NOT in the package (only SAS/Stata code and logs), so replication requires IBES, CRSP and SDC access.
design_notes: Package replication_package_MS-ACC-21-00096: readme.pdf (data memo + dictionary), 'IPO 04082022 Forecast.sas' (builds forecast-level DiD sample from IBES detail, CRSP, SDC IPO dates; treat=1 if brokerage has an IPO date; ipo_pre1/ipo_post1 = within 365 days before/after; ipo_prepost1 = either), 'IPO 04082022 Non-Forecast.sas' (recommendations, broker-year and analyst panels), Gen_DinD_04082022_IPO.do (Stata regressions for Tables 3-11, Figures 1-2 via coefplot of ipo_pre23 ipo_prepost1 ipo_post23 ipo_post4x), and three log files with full regression output (IPO_stata_log.log contains coefficients and N for every table). No .dta or .sas7bdat files shipped.
main_or_robustness: main (Table 3) / Table 7 is a secondary broker-level analysis

specs.switch_off_caveat: ipo_prepost1 is a temporary +/-1-year window indicator around the brokerage IPO; it is 0 again from the second post-IPO year. Eligible only under the protocol's switch-off rule (drop post-adoption broker-years with treatment = 0, Hull fn. 6).
specs.outcome: ln_numfirms (log number of firms covered by the brokerage in year t)
specs.treatment_definition: 1 for IPO brokerages in the two-year window around the brokerage IPO (year before and year after; forecasts within 30 days of the IPO deleted), 0 otherwise (SAS: ipo_pre1 or ipo_post1)
specs.sample_condition: broker-year panel ipo_11162021_broker (N=6,374 with broker FE, 762 brokers)
specs.data_file: ipo_11162021_broker.dta (NOT shipped; built by 'IPO 04082022 Non-Forecast.sas' from IBES/SDC)
specs.notes: Columns 1-3 use year FE only; columns 4-6 add the time-invariant treat indicator (no broker FE).

specs.exclusion_reason: time-varying controls (ln_numanalystbroker ln_horizon ln_numfirmscov ln_firmexp) in every forecast-level column; treatment is a temporary window
specs.notes: Tables 4, 5, 9, 10, 11 are variants (alternative FE/clusters, pre/post window dummies ipo_pre23 ipo_post23 ipo_post4x, subgroup splits), all with the same controls.

data_access: proprietary (IBES, CRSP, SDC via WRDS; no data files in package)
screener_notes: Eligibility hinges on treating the +/-1-year IPO window as an adoption with later switch-off (protocol 5b). If the lead prefers to treat a by-construction temporary window as a different estimand, reclassify as near-miss. Full text unavailable; Table 7 column numbering inferred from the do-file order (3 outcomes x 3 FE structures). No data shipped, so the paper cannot be replicated from the package regardless.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Brokerage IPO dates span the 31-year IBES sample; exact number of IPO years cannot be determined without the data (SDC-based). Log shows 762 brokers and 6,374 broker-years in the broker FE regressions.
preferred_spec_note: Among eligible specs only; the paper's headline results are the forecast-level Table 3 (ineligible).
